newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal to invest $3.8 billion in rail plan.
newsitem.headline: Portugal to invest $3.8 billion in rail plan.

text.p: Portugal's state railway will invest some 600 billion escudos ($3.8 billion) in a three-year restructuring plan under which it will be split in two and private firms allowed to run some operations, the government said on Monday.

From February, the heavily loss-making CP-Caminhos de Ferro Portugueses will cease to exist. It will be replaced by an operating company for passenger and freight services and another for infrastructure, Planning Minister Joao Cravinho said.
The plan also calls for the creation of a watchdog to monitor the activities of the two concerns, Cravinho told a news conference to present members of the new railway board.

Cravinho said that part of the plan, which includes investment in new lines and equipment, would be financed directly by the state with the remainder being covered by European Union loans and borrowing.
The minister said that the infrastructure company, so far unnamed, would operate in the national network, lines, the rolling stock and signals.
The other company, CP-Transportes, would operate the suburban and long-distance passenger and freight traffic.
"CP-Transportes is going to function efficiently in competition with other private operators who want to operate the rail links," he said.
The restructuring of the state railway would clear the way for private companies to handle some services, acting as sub-contractors or in partnership with state companies.
"The railway is going to be open to whoever wants to take part...to provide transport services," Cravinho said.

"This possibility (sub-contracting) will happen. At the same time, there will regional lines. If there were interest, they could be exploited in partnership with public and private concerns," he said.
The railway loses around one billion escudos a week and Cravinho said that it would continue in the red through 1998, at least.
"Only in 1999 will the first positive signs, in financial terms, of the restructuring will begin to appear," he said.
The minister said that he had asked new chairman Manuel Frasquilho to order a thorough audit of all the rail company's subsidiary concerns.

The reorganisation has been opposed by unions but a 24-hour strike planned to start at midnight on December 23 was called off to give the new management team time to discuss the plan with employees, labour leaders said. ($ = 156.3 Portugese Escudos)
